item.title: Hiker, 61, battles agonizing injury on grueling climb, resets dislocated shoulder himself
item.description: Kurt Siuzdak slipped on wet granite on New Hampshire's Mount Washington, dislocated his shoulder, popped it back in and kept climbing to the top.
item.content:encoded:
A 61-year-old hiker popped his own dislocated shoulder back into place during a hike on New Hampshire's Mount Washington — and kept climbing.

Connecticut resident Kurt Siuzdak was hiking Mount Washington earlier this week when he suffered the painful injury after slipping on wet granite.

The news was reported by The Boston Globe on Thursday, citing a Wednesday statement from the New Hampshire Fish and Game Department.

HUSBAND AND WIFE GET TRAPPED IN PREMIER HIKING DESTINATION; ONLY ONE OF THEM MAKES IT OUT ALIVE

Siuzdak began hiking at around 4 a.m. on Tuesday, according to the report.

Six hours later, at around 10 a.m., he slipped on a wet granite slab in a section called the Lakes of the Clouds.

In the fall, he dislocated his shoulder and injured his back.

About a mile and a half from the summit of Mount Washington, Siuzdak decided to keep going — slowly and steadily. 

CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER

He was found by another hiker about five hours later.

Siuzdak told rescuers he planned to press on and "figure out his options" once he reached the summit, as the Globe noted.

When two officers hiked down to meet him at around 5 p.m., Siuzdak was still making his way up the mountain at a slow pace, officials said.

Flanked by the two officers, Siuzdak kept climbing.

He eventually reached the summit under his own power.

After being evaluated by emergency personnel, he asked to be taken to his car so he could drive himself to urgent care, the Globe reported.

At some point during the hike, Siuzdak managed to reset his dislocated shoulder himself, officials said.

In a statement, the New Hampshire Fish and Game Department highlighted Siuzdak's preparedness.

The agency noted he had followed the agency's recommendations by packing extra gear, including warm clothing and a first aid kit.

"These items turned out to be much needed after his accident, and he was thankful that he had heeded the recommendations," officials said, according to The Boston Globe.

Fox News Digital reached out to Siuzdak for comment.

Fox News Digital also reached out to the New Hampshire Fish and Game Department for comment.

item.title: Paramount appears to learn from its 'Big Brother' racial double standard on 'The Challenge'
item.description: Three contestants were removed from MTV's "The Challenge: Cutthroat" after a reported racial incident involving the N-word and a code of conduct breach.
item.content:encoded:
Three contestants were abruptly removed from MTV’s long-running athletic reality competition series "The Challenge" this week following a reported racial incident that the show chose not to air.

At the beginning of Wednesday’s episode of "The Challenge: Cutthroat," host T.J. Lavin entered the house without Leo Dionicio, Josh Goldstein and Nelson Thomas present.

"Leo, Nelson and Josh all broke the code of conduct here on 'The Challenge,' so they're all gone," Lavin told the remaining contestants.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The show did not air the incident that led to the three disqualifications or provide any additional details.

Page Six reported that Dionicio, who is Black, used the N-word during a game and Goldstein, who is White, repeated it. According to the report, Thomas became angry over Goldstein’s use of the word and later damaged the kitchen. Production then removed all three contestants.

The Paramount+ original is the 42nd season of the long-running MTV franchise. "The Challenge" is generally classified as reality television, but the modern version is built around athletic competition. Contestants run, swim, climb, wrestle, carry heavy weight and race through obstacle courses that test strength, endurance and mental toughness. Seasons typically end with a grueling final that can stretch across multiple days and resemble an adventure race more than a reality show.

The controversy also bears a striking resemblance to one Paramount faced three years ago on another reality competition show. The company appears to have learned from a racial double standard it applied back then.

Thomas subsequently confirmed at least part of the reported account.

"I let my emotions take over, broke dishes, destroyed [the] kitchen and violated the code of conduct," Thomas wrote on X. "That’s on me."

Thomas also claimed that Goldstein apologized to him privately and urged Goldstein to address the situation publicly.

"Saying you have Black friends doesn’t give you a pass to use the N-word," Thomas wrote.

Dionicio, meanwhile, discussed his removal during an appearance on fellow "Challenge" competitor Johnny "Bananas" Devenanzio’s "Death, Taxes and Bananas" podcast.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

At the beginning of the discussion, Devenanzio said they had been instructed "from the top" not to reveal the specifics of the incident. Despite that, Dionicio argued that he did not deserve to be included in the mass disqualification.

"I was really, really upset because what was said was super ignorant," Dionicio said. "I thought the hand I was dealt was pretty messed up considering I didn’t really do s--- wrong."

Dionicio said he believed one contestant should have been fined, another should have been removed and he should not have been punished at all.

Johnny "Bananas" pushed back on Dionicio’s argument.

"I think what’s understood is that they have to have a rule, and it has to apply to everybody equally," he said.

Later in the conversation, however, Dionicio acknowledged that every contestant had signed the same agreement.

"I know we all signed the same contract," Dionicio said. "It’s just frustrating because I didn’t really think that would apply to me. But then I realized, you know, I’m not bigger than the program, unfortunately."

Dionicio never explicitly said, "I’m Black, so I should be allowed to use the N-word." But taken together, his comments strongly suggest that is his position. He reportedly used the word, said he did not believe the rule should have applied to him and then emphasized in a separate post on X that he is Black and Afro-Latino.

Paramount declined to discuss the specific actions that led to each contestant’s removal. A source familiar with the production said Bunim/Murray Productions has a clear code of conduct and that all three cast members were removed after violating it. The source directed OutKick to Thomas’ public comments about the incident.

The response did not confirm whether Dionicio and Goldstein were removed for using the same word or whether the same provision was applied to both contestants. But Paramount also did not dispute the reported account or challenge OutKick’s interpretation that the rule was enforced equally. Dionicio and Goldstein did not respond to requests for comment prior to publication.

In August 2023, CBS removed "Big Brother" contestant Luke Valentine after he used the N-word inside the house. The network said Valentine violated the show’s code of conduct and that it had "zero tolerance" for the use of a racial slur.

Except, as OutKick reported at the time, another contestant, Kirsten Elwin, had used the same word days earlier and received no apparent punishment.

Valentine is White. Elwin is Black.

At the time, I wrote that CBS could not claim to have a zero-tolerance rule while applying different consequences based on the race of the person who violated it.

I wasn’t arguing that a White person and a Black person using the N-word carry the same social meaning because they don’t.

But a television production’s code of conduct is either a rule or it isn’t. If contestants are told that a particular word is prohibited, their skin color should not determine whether the rule applies to them.

CBS and MTV were both under the Paramount umbrella when the "Big Brother" incident occurred, just as they are now. This time, the company appears to have applied the standard equally.

Again, Paramount’s refusal to explain the disqualifications prevents us from saying that definitively. But the available reporting indicates that Dionicio and Goldstein used the same word and were both removed from the competition. Dionicio’s subsequent comments suggest he believed being Black should have changed how the rule applied to him.

If the reported account is accurate, production enforced the rule against everyone rather than determining who was socially entitled to violate its conduct policy.

Paramount deserves credit for apparently correcting the double standard it applied on "Big Brother" in 2023. Now it should be transparent enough to confirm that equal enforcement is exactly what happened.

item.title: Trump announces White House ban against three media outlets
item.description: President Donald Trump announced CNN, MS NOW and Politico are banned from the White House, dubbing them "fake news" and teased other outlets could follow.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico will be banned from the White House.

"I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW ... and Politico ... from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

Trump doubled down on his announced ban while taking questions from reporters at the Oval Office, citing "cumulative stories" the three outlets have published over the years.

"You get sick of it," Trump said.

CNN FIRES BACK AT TRUMP WHITE HOUSE OVER ATTACKS ON REPORTER, CALLS THEM 'BENEATH THE OFFICE'

Trump denied he was trying to intimidate the press from doing its job in an exchange with another reporter.

For decades, CNN has been part of a rotating pool of five networks, including Fox News, that travel with the president around the world.

Notably, CNN has already been selected to lead network pool coverage Monday as Trump is set to attend the United Nations General Assembly.

TRUMP BLASTS NEW YORK TIMES, CNN FOR 'SEDITIOUS' COVERAGE OF IRAN WAR

Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the Republican Arkansas governor and former White House press secretary during the first Trump administration, was in attendance at the Oval Office event focused on healthcare and rejected the notion that Trump opposes a free press that's enshrined in the First Amendment of the Constitution.

"I think it's hard for you to argue against a free press when you're literally standing in the Oval Office asking questions of the president of the United States," Sanders told reporters. "He has been more accessible and easier to talk to than any president in history."

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Past efforts by the Trump administration to ban outlets and individual journalists have been blocked by federal judges.

"I don't think that a court should allow fake news to be written day, after day, after day. I think that somebody has a right to keep them away," Trump said.

Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy said CNN was still broadcasting live from its tent on media row outside the White House, but a senior White House official told him top brass at CNN, MS NOW and Politico were being informed that their journalists cannot be on White House grounds beginning Saturday.

"CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting," the network said in a statement on X. "We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government. Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right."

Politico also issued a statement, telling Fox News Digital, "Politico will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones. We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them."

A spokesperson for MS NOW declined to comment.

item.title: Vance calls midterms a referendum on ‘common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy'
item.description: JD Vance rallied in Iowa, calling the midterms a referendum on common sense and targeting Democrats he says have abandoned the working man.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance called out Democrats Friday, saying the midterms will be a referendum on "common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy."

While stumping in Iowa, Vance said Democrats are no longer "the party my grandparents grew up talking about."

Raised by a union steelworker, Vance said his father told him that "FDR’s Democrat party, that JFK’s Democrat party was the party of the workingman.

THE ONE LINE FROM JD VANCE’S GOP KEYNOTE THAT REVEALS HIS VISION FOR AMERICA

"This is not FDR’s party, as much as we might wish it was. It's not JFK’s party. Ladies and gentlemen, it’s not even Bill Clinton’s party."

Vance said today’s Democrats don’t believe the country needs to be "built upon" but "utterly transformed."

"In New York," he said, some of the midterm candidates are calling for the "total eradication of Western civilization. Somebody running for Congress in New York — and I promise I’m not joking about this — said that July Fourth is actually about the liberation of Palestine and Puerto Rico."

To loud boos, Vance said, "You could almost laugh about" the idea of Thomas Jefferson writing the Declaration of Independence and thinking about the liberation of Palestine and Puerto Rico.

MORNING GLORY: FIVE SENATE RACES SHOW WHY DEMOCRATS MAY REGRET THEIR PRIMARY CHOICES

"But, unfortunately, it’s not funny because those people are dead serious, and this election is a referendum on common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy. Let’s send the crazy packing and get them out of Washington, D.C." Vance said to cheers.

Vance also claimed some Democratic candidates are "out-and-out lunatics" who have "lost their ever-loving minds."

"These are the ones who will tell you that our history is evil, and this country needs to be bulldozed and started over from the beginning," he continued.

'JESUS WAS A RADICAL': PROGRESSIVES INVOKE CHRIST TO SELL LEFT-WING AGENDA ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL

But he said other Democrat candidates are "smart enough to realize that the country hasn't lost its mind, and, so, they try to be just a little bit more subtle."

Calling out Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Adam Hamilton of Kansas, Vance claimed Hamilton gave off a "kind of ‘gee whiz, I’m a nice pastor’ vibe," but he's a man that tells his congregation not about the gospel of Jesus Christ, but that they need to repent for their White privilege."

Recent polls have shown a tightening race between Hamilton and GOP incumbent Kansas Sen. Roger Marshall.

During the rally, Vance threw his support behind Iowa Republicans, including gubernatorial nominee Zach Lane, Rep. Ashley Hinson and congressional candidate Chris McGowan.

item.title: Taylor Swift quiet as friend Ed Sheeran takes heat over Macklemore's 'Free Palestine' concert fiasco
item.description: Taylor Swift's silence on Ed Sheeran's Macklemore controversy raises questions as the fallout over "Free Palestine" chants continues to escalate.
item.content:encoded:
Taylor Swift hasn’t publicly spoken out in support of close friend Ed Sheeran as controversy over Macklemore's removal has engulfed Sheeran's latest tour.

Sheeran has faced scrutiny from some pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel activists after his tour promoter and venues dropped rapper Macklemore from his Loop Tour after Macklemore’s onstage chants of "Free Palestine" earlier this month.

Groups, including StopAntisemitism and the Combat Antisemitism Movement called for Macklemore's removal, while singer Pink criticized Macklemore's performance.

MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE

It was during his opening set on the tour at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium when the Grammy-winning Macklemore also described Israel’s actions using terms such as "genocide" and "apartheid."

Since the dust-up, Sheeran released a statement addressing the situation, saying the decision to remove Macklemore was made by the tour’s promoters and venues, not by him personally. He also noted his desire to continue the tour and not let down fans or crew members who rely on his concerts for their income.

That was followed by four of his tour openers withdrawing from his concerts in solidarity with Macklemore, while also noting their own opposition to what they described as genocide in Gaza. Macklemore notably drew fierce criticism in 2014 when he donned what appeared to be an antisemitic costume caricaturing Jewish people, although he claimed it was unintentional. 

As Sheeran has been navigating one of the most public controversies of his career, his longtime friend and collaborator Swift has been quiet, reflective of a career where she's generally, but not always, stayed out of political strife.

ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL

Swift has shared a close personal and professional relationship with Sheeran spanning more than a decade. It has even been described as one of the most high-profile friendships in modern music history, with the pair mutually supporting each other through the years and collaborating both in the studio and onstage.

Sheeran appeared as the opening act for the North American leg of Swift’s "Red Tour" in 2013, and the two have teamed up on songs including the duet "Everything Has Changed" from that tour and the 2021 song "Run." He also was a "surprise guest" during her Eras Tour.

Plenty of other memorable moments have ensued between the two. When Swift won her first BRIT Award in 2015, she publicly thanked Sheeran in her acceptance speech, crediting him with teaching her about British culture and pubs. Sheeran has been known to appear at her concerts, one time dressed as a clown as he went onto the stage during one of her Nashville shows. Both artists have often described how they’re able to relate to one another because of the unique pressures they experience at their level of fame.

Swift’s reps are known for protecting the singer’s brand, and Swift has historically been selective about when she speaks out, but she has used her platform to advocate for some progressive causes in recent years, such as endorsing Kamala Harris and supporting gay rights. She also has tried to get more voters registered, including when she endorsed Harris in 2024.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

In 2018, Swift criticized Republican Tennessee Senate candidate Marsha Blackburn over her conservative voting record and opposition to LGBTQ+ and women’s rights, instead endorsing her Democratic opponent, former Tennessee Gov. Phil Bredesen.

She also described President Donald Trump as a poor leader during the COVID-19 pandemic and accused him of cheating to win.

Some who've worked in the entertainment industry think it's best for performers to remain quiet about politics, whether it's Macklemore, Swift or any other celebrity.

"My general feeling is they ought to stay in their own lane," David Sams, CEO of Sam’s Global Companies, a conglomerate of media networks and talent management, and former head of global marketing and creative affairs at King World, told Fox News Digital. 

"It’s a lot of noise, and with everything going on in the world right now, to even give five seconds to their shenanigans is ridiculous."

Swift has also at times been criticized by the left for being insufficiently outspoken on issues.

Fox News Digital reached out to Swift for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: 'He's Dust': Ole Miss students rip Lane Kiffin as LSU coach prepares for hatred in Oxford
item.description: Ole Miss students didn't hold back in The Grove, directing fiery trash talk at Lane Kiffin ahead of his first trip back to Oxford as LSU coach.
item.content:encoded:
OXFORD, Miss. — Ole Miss fans have been waiting for this game since Lane Kiffin left town 10 months ago for LSU, so one more day won't hurt. But that doesn’t mean the animosity toward their former head coach in Oxford has to simmer down before kickoff.

It took me around five minutes of traversing campus to start hearing the banter about the guy who used to roam the Rebels' sidelines for six years.

As he makes his way back to Oxford on Saturday afternoon to lead his Tigers into hostile territory, it's pretty obvious that a large percentage of the fan base still holds a grudge for the way in which Lane Kiffin bolted town after Thanksgiving last year, and just two weeks before the College Football Playoff was set to begin.

LANE KIFFIN’S RETURN TO OLE MISS COMES WITH BETRAYAL, LAWSUITS AND MEMORIES OF HIM TRYING TO BURN IT ALL DOWN

"Man, I'm not gonna lie. F--- Lane Kiffin. Lane Kiffin's 'K', we smokin him bro, no cap," one Ole Miss student said inside "The Grove" on Friday afternoon.

He wasn’t alone in his thoughts, as you could imagine around the Ole Miss campus.

"Man, he's dust," another Ole Miss student exclaimed. "He's nothing but dust. He's defiantly scheming, he knows what he's doing, whether that's putting Leavitt on the injury report, he's f---ing playing. He's just a scumbag."

On a beautiful, but hot, Friday afternoon in Oxford, fans flooded the historic Square located in the middle of downtown Oxford for some good eats and drinking.

The party atmosphere started on Wednesday night, and I don't imagine this thing comes to an end until sometime Sunday afternoon. No matter what takes place on the field inside Vaught Hemingway Stadium on Saturday evening, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin will be at the forefront of a hostile environment.

At this point, fans were expecting nothing less.

MOUNTED POLICE, EXTRA PATROLS AND KIFFIN HATE: OXFORD PREPARES FOR OLE MISS-LSU GAME WITH EXTRA SECURITY

Months of talking through social media, Vanity Fair, podcasts and interviews, Lane Kiffin is clearly enjoying the attention that he's garnering before this showdown with his former team.

And, if any one thinks different, you don't know Kiffin. Think of it as a professional wrestler drawing boos from a crowded arena. Now, think of Lane playing the role of Hulk Hogan's NWO persona.

Everything is a show, and Kiffin is selling advertisement for his return to Oxford.

Think about what took place earlier this week when the LSU head coach put Sam Leavitt on the initial injury report, listing him as 'doubtful', before upgrading him to 'questionable' on Thursday evening.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding wasn’t buying it, not for one minute.

"Well, I got the text before the report went out from Lane, like 'Hey, our quarterback's out,'" Golding mentioned to Pat McAfee. "I'm like, 'Ok buddy, I bet he is.' I've been around here a lot of Wednesday’s with you man for three and half years. I said, I think our first one had 42 guys on the first ever SEC injury report on a Wednesday.

"So, I was like, 'Yea man, see ya Saturday.'"

There will be trash talking that takes place on Saturday that would make a standup comedian blush.

Most of it will be directed at Lane Kiffin, while LSU fans will undoubtedly take some of the heat on deflection.

But, this is what makes college football so great. A wild day around the campus of Ole Miss awaits, along with the official arrival of the most hated man in the state of Mississippi.

item.title: Unsealed FBI interviews reveal Obama, Emanuel's discussions about Blagojevich Senate seat deal
item.description: Newly unsealed FBI interviews reveal what Barack Obama and Rahm Emanuel told agents about Rod Blagojevich's plans for the Illinois Senate seat.
item.content:encoded:
Anyone who has a conversation with former Illinois Gov. Rod Blagojevich is likely to hear his claim that he was never going to sell the U.S. Senate seat vacated by former President Barack Obama in 2008, insisting his innocence in the high-profile case that led to him serving nearly eight years in federal prison. 

Blagojevich has repeated for years that he was closing in on a deal to appoint Lisa Madigan to the U.S. Senate.

Hers is a name that has largely dropped out of the public arena. At the time of the scandal, Madigan served as Illinois attorney general. More relevant to this case, she is the daughter of the very powerful and entrenched then-Speaker of the Illinois House Mike Madigan. 

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

The former speaker has since gone to prison for a separate corruption case. (Welcome to Illinois.) Blagojevich claims he would have appointed Lisa to the Senate in exchange for the father supporting his healthcare package and budget.

Shortly after the arrest of Gov. Blagojevich in December 2009, both President-elect Obama and his incoming chief of staff, Rahm Emanuel, were interviewed by the FBI. Obama was interviewed Dec. 18, nine days after the governor was arrested. Emanuel was interviewed on the 20th. The records of those interviews were kept out of both criminal trials and away from the public, until now. Fox News has obtained the partially redacted FBI FD-302s of those interviews.

The Obama interview notes, "Obama was asked whether he was aware of Emanuel having a conversation with the Blagojevich administration regarding Lisa Madigan being considered for the Senate seat in exchange for legislation being passed.

"Emanuel would have been aware that Lisa Madigan was an acceptable candidate to Obama. Emanuel had an open line of conversation with the Blagojevich administration."

The Emanuel interview notes that, on Dec. 8, 2008, "(David) Axelrod and Emanuel went to see (U.S. Senator Dick) Durbin, D-Ill. In this meeting, they all agreed that Lisa Madigan would be a good candidate.

"As a result of this conversation, Emanuel contacted (Blagojevich Chief of staff, John) Harris and told him the merits of appointing Lisa Madigan as Senator."

The next morning, Dec. 9, 2009, just after 6 a.m., Blagojevich was arrested at his home in Chicago.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS ‘BERNIE BROS’ COULD SINK DEMOCRATS BY SADDLING MODERATES WITH SOCIALIST AGENDA

Then-U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois Patrick Fitzgerald said, "Governor Blagojevich was arrested in the middle of what we can only describe as a political corruption crime spree. We acted to stop that crime spree."

"That just proves the Madigan deal was very much front and center. It was something I was about to do," Blagojevich said in light of the newly unsealed information. "There never was a crime spree that Mr. Fitzgerald, the U.S. attorney, said he was stopping to justify arresting a sitting governor in his home."

Other interesting notes from the interviews: President Obama initially wanted Valerie Jarrett to succeed him in the Senate. But he reversed his thinking early in the process, deciding "that he would like Jarrett to join him at the White House as a senior advisor."

However, "Emanuel was still interested in Jarrett taking the Senate seat rather than working in the White House."

Because, according to the Emanuel interview, "the fact that she is the president-elect’s best friend, having her on the White House staff would be awkward."

"Rahm’s a crafty, political, crafty, cunning and very effective political operator," Blagojevich chimed in. "He was interested in being closer to the king."

Eventually, according to the Emanuel interview, Obama became resolute. 

"Obama told Emanuel he made a decision that Jarrett was going to the White House, and he was not going to reconsider this decision."

After that, a gaggle of familiar names entered the ring for consideration: Tammy Duckworth, and Reps. Jan Schakowsky, D-Ill., and Rep. Jesse Jackson Jr., D-Ill., who also went to prison for a separate case.

MINNESOTA FRAUD SCANDAL WILL HAUNT FLANAGAN IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE RACE, TOP HOUSE REPUBLICAN WARNS

Then Obama, busy with establishing a new administration, stated, "He did not want to put his thumb on the scale."

Still, he dispatched Emanuel to communicate with the governor’s office that "Obama was interested in someone who he thought would be a good senator for the people of Illinois and who could also hold the seat in the 2010 election."

Blagojevich ended up appointing Roland Burris to Obama’s vacated seat. Burris did not run for re-election.

Republican Mark Kirk won the seat in 2010 and was defeated by Tammy Duckworth in 2016.

Blagojevich served 7 years, 11 months in prison until President Trump commuted his sentence in 2020. Blagojevich received a full pardon in 2025.

Fox News reached out to both former President Obama and Rahm Emanuel. They did not respond.

item.title: Illegal immigrant rideshare driver charged with rape in Maryland had prior NYC sex abuse arrest
item.description: Abdoulaye Dia, an Empower rideshare driver, had a prior New York sex abuse arrest before he allegedly raped a teen passenger in Silver Spring.
item.content:encoded:
An illegal immigrant rideshare driver accused of sexually assaulting a teenage female passenger in Maryland has a history of sex abuse in New York, federal authorities said.

Abdoulaye Dia, of Lanham, Maryland, was charged with first-degree rape, kidnapping, second-degree assault and third-degree sex offense, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said.

On Tuesday, Montgomery County Police officers were called to a hospital where an underage teen girl reported a rape. She told police she was raped by an Empower rideshare driver.

RIDESHARE DRIVER ARRESTED IN ALLEGED SCHEME TARGETING IVY LEAGUE STUDENTS FOR SEX: PROSECUTORS

Dia, a citizen of Guinea, took her to a parking lot in Silver Spring, where the alleged assault occurred.

Investigators identified Dia through information obtained from the rideshare app. He was arrested Wednesday.

TWICE-DEPORTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH RAPE AS DHS URGES FAIRFAX TO HONOR ICE DETAINER

Empower told Fox News Digital that all its drivers undergo background, sex offender, motor vehicle, and Social Security traces. Furthermore, they are vetted against the same global watchlist used by Uber and Lyft, through the exact same screening provider.

"The background check, sex offender check, driving record check, social security trace, and global watchlist search on this customer were conducted on July 16, 2026 and did not reveal any incidents," the company said about Dia. "The Montgomery County Police Department reached out to Empower about this incident. Empower, as is our policy, asked law enforcement what Empower could do to assist their investigation and immediately provided all information requested."

Dia was previously arrested June 10 in New York City for sexual abuse by forcible compulsion, forcible touching of the sexual/intimate parts of another person, injuring a child less than 17 and sexual abuse without consent, a DHS spokesperson told Fox News.

He entered the United States illegally through Arizona in December 2023 and was released by the Biden administration, DHS said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Empower for comment.

item.title: Trump declares victory in historic deal with Greenland as he secures 'permanent' US military rights
item.description: President Donald Trump's Greenland deal bars China and Russia from the Arctic island and grants permanent U.S. military basing with no expiration.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump struck a sweeping agreement with Denmark and Greenland this week granting the United States permanent military rights on the strategically placed Arctic island.

The U.S. will now have permanent access, basing and overflight rights in Greenland and the ability to establish additional military installations as needed, according to a senior U.S. official who outlined the deal exclusively to Fox News Digital.

The deal bars China, Russia and other non-NATO countries from establishing military bases or maintaining troops in Greenland. It also restricts adversaries from investing in sensitive sectors that could pose a threat to U.S. national security.

"This historic deal is a huge win for the United States and the American people," Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News Digital. "Thanks to President Trump’s vision and leadership, this historic agreement permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer.

DENMARK VOWS TO DEFEND GREENLAND AFTER TRUMP REITERATES US SHOULD CONTROL TERRITORY

"Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area," Rubio said. "This deal permanently and completely addresses our national security concerns in Greenland.

The new agreement, which has no expiration date, stops short of transferring sovereignty over Greenland to the U.S. But administration officials still view its permanence as key to addressing the security concerns that drove Trump's push to acquire the territory in the first place.

"The difference here is we're not spending any money for the right" to expand the U.S. military presence, the senior official explained.

The deal is designed to remain in effect even if Greenland eventually becomes an independent country, they added.

"For over 100 years, Presidents have known the strategic importance of Greenland, but NONE of them were able to do anything about it. I am proud to be the President that permanently and conclusively addressed this very important situation. This is an "Infinite Life" Agreement, there is no end!" Trump wrote on Truth Social Friday. 

Fox News Digital reached out to the governments of Greenland and Denmark for comment.

Trump had repeatedly argued that control of Greenland was necessary for U.S. national security, pointing to the island's strategic location in the Arctic as Russia and China expand their presence and capabilities in the region.

The deal significantly expands on the longstanding U.S. defense relationship with Greenland. The U.S. already operates Pituffik Space Base and has maintained military access to the island under a defense agreement dating back to 1951.

Under the new agreement, however, Denmark and Greenland would not have approval authority over additional U.S. military installations. The U.S. would consult with them but would have the right to build new installations when it determines they are necessary without needing their buy-in, the official said.

The administration believes an expanded U.S. military footprint in Greenland could eventually play a role in Trump's planned Golden Dome missile defense system.

"We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many. We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction," Trump added. 

RUSSIA’S QUIETER NUCLEAR SUBMARINES THREATEN NATO, FORMER COMMANDER WARNS

The deal only allows the U.S. and its allies to make "sensitive investments" on the island, such as telecommunications infrastructure, undersea cables, ports and critical minerals.

The administration is seeking to prevent Greenland from becoming another version of what it sees as the strategic vulnerability that developed around the Panama Canal, where Chinese commercial interests have fueled U.S. concerns that ostensibly civilian infrastructure could have national security implications.

"We're never going to face that in Greenland as a result of this," the official told Fox News Digital.

Officials from both Greenland and Denmark, which holds sovereignty over the self-governing island territory, initially scoffed at Trump’s insistence that the U.S. must "own" Greenland.

But months of negotiations between Rubio, White House advisor Stephen Miller and officials at the State Department and National Security Council led to a deal that satisfied all sides, a second official told Fox News Digital.

Representatives from all three countries went through "various rounds of quiet negotiations that never leaked and never got out there" starting in February, as Denmark and Greenland came to see the agreement as serving their own security interests.

"They recognize, at the end of the day, that they have a national security concern here as well," Rubio said. "Denmark and Greenland understand that they don't have the financial means necessary to defend Greenland if it were to come under attack or be threatened. The United States has the power to do that."

item.title: Pro-life vs socialism: GOP lawmakers divided over controversial guaranteed income programs
item.description: The Mother & Infant Cash Coalition says conservative lawmakers are backing direct cash transfers for mothers and newborns on pro-family grounds.
item.content:encoded:
Although guaranteed income programs have faced partisan pushback nationwide since gaining national traction in 2018, a growing faction of conservatives is finding common ground with direct cash initiatives centered on mothers and newborns.

According to Tegan Lecheler, national program director for the Mother and Infant Cash Coalition (MICC), the "common-sense" nature of early childhood cash transfers has prompted conservative lawmakers and advocates to reach out to her organization in support.

"I think we're in a really polarized time politically right now," Lecheler told Fox News Digital. "We are not a political organization and want to work to improve families' outcomes. We believe an effective strategy for doing that is to build a big tent – a wide tent with a lot of people underneath it."

EXCLUSIVE: PENCE GROUP KNOCKS VANCE PLAN TO PAY STAY-AT-HOME PARENTS UP TO $9K PER CHILD

Lecheler noted that early childhood support aligns with pro-family conservative principles.

"Some of the solutions that we're putting forward really resonate with have been folks who agree that people should be able to have families that look the way they want," Lecheler said. "There are certain factions that are excited by the idea of cash transfers specifically within the period surrounding the birth of a child because it enables families to have the number of kids that they want to have."

Founded in 2023, the Mother and Infant Cash Coalition grew out of a broader movement toward direct financial support for young families. Lecheler, who previously managed operations with The Bridge Project — an unrestricted cash transfer initiative launched in 2021 that operates across 14 red, blue, and purple states — noted that momentum for direct cash assistance built rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Advocates and researchers increasingly argue that flexible cash benefits offer a more cost-effective way to improve family stability than traditional, highly restricted in-kind welfare programs.

As direct cash initiatives expanded, organizations focused specifically on the perinatal period — from pregnancy through early infancy — began coordinating nationwide. That collaboration formed the Mother and Infant Cash Coalition, which aims to leverage early-childhood cash transfers to strengthen family stability and drive better maternal and child health outcomes. Member organizations include the Magnolia Mother’s Trust (MMT), launched in 2018, which provides selected Black mothers with $1,000 per month in unconditional cash for a full year.

Mayors for a Guaranteed Income, a coalition of over 150 mayors, bids to solve the affordability crisis with cash handouts. The coalition is responsible for over 100 pilot programs launched since 2018 and the establishment of the program in Cook County, Illinois, which was the first municipality to expand a guaranteed income program permanently.

Despite fierce national pushback against guaranteed basic income (GBI) programs — which opponents often criticize as "lottery socialism" — Lecheler stresses that conservative interest often stems from fiscal pragmatic arguments.

"There are other folks who are excited about it from sort of an efficiency angle, and think about this work because it is a lower administrative burden," Lecheler told Fox News Digital. "It is also more cost-effective to prevent poor birth outcomes like low birth weight or preterm birth than it is to respond to them after the fact."

MAYORS WANT TO KEEP HANDING OUT FREE CASH AFTER FEDERAL FUNDS DRIED UP

The debate over early cash aid reached a flashpoint in Michigan over "Rx Kids," a citywide bipartisan initiative providing expectant mothers with a lump-sum payment of $1,500 during pregnancy, followed by $500 per month for up to 12 months post-birth. While Rx Kids is not a member of the Mother and Infant Cash Coalition, it operates on a similar direct-cash model.

Michigan House Republicans launched a formal inquiry into the initiative, which has absorbed more than $300 million in combined public and private funding. House Oversight Committee Chairman Rep. Jay DeBoyer, R-Clay Township, criticized the program's lack of oversight, arguing it functions as a "redistribution of wealth" that fails to solve systemic poverty without spending guardrails.

However, other Michigan Republicans view the policy through a pro-life lens. State Sen. John Damoose, R-Harbor Springs, publicly broke with critics to endorse the initiative.

"Helping moms and babies truly fits into the call of Jesus," Damoose wrote in an op-ed for the Detroit Free Press. "I believe in the sanctity of life. I believe we need to be champions for the unborn. That means more than just calling ourselves ‘pro-life’ — it means doing everything we can to make it easier for expectant moms to choose life. It means being there for families from the very beginning — and offering them the resources they need to thrive."

MICHIGAN REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER WARNS GUARANTEED INCOME PROGRAMS DO NOT WORK, VOICES OPPOSITION TO STATE POLICY

Similar policy rifts are playing out nationwide as conservative lawmakers evaluate direct cash policies alongside conservative economic priorities.

"We have people from the right that have organically reached out to us to voice support," Lecheler noted, pointing to conservative support for policies like the Federal Child Tax Credit (CTC) and proposals to expand Child Care and Development Fund assistance.

A spokesperson for the Economic Securities Project (ESP), an organization that led the creation of more than 100 guaranteed income programs, told Fox News Digital that affordability is a growing issue among Americans, calling for the need of direct cash.

"Cash assistance is widely supported across party lines, and we see that with the proliferation of cash proposals at the federal level, continued support for different versions of the CTC, as well as promising pilots like Rx Kids and the ASCEND program in New Mexico," Shafeka Hashash, director of Cash Initiatives at Economic Security Project (ESP), told Fox News Digital. 

"Growing concerns about the cost-of-living crisis and how AI will impact the workforce are also driving bipartisan support for cash."

IOWA SUPERVISOR SLAMS BAN ON GUARANTEED INCOME PROGRAMS AS STATE ‘WAGING IDEOLOGICAL WARS’

Nevertheless, major state-level legal and legislative efforts to restrict or eliminate cash transfer programs continue in red states:

As of 2026, four red states — Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, and South Dakota — have enacted laws banning or restricting local guaranteed income and unconditional cash-aid programs. In addition, Kansas passed similar restrictive legislation when a bill became law without the governor's signature.

To date, Cook County remains the primary local municipality to enact a permanent guaranteed basic income program. For advocates like Lecheler, the policy push comes down to basic economic survival for young families.

"In the richest country in the world, I feel strongly that families shouldn't have to work three or four jobs just to keep food on the table," Lecheler said.

item.title: Olympic swimmer Réka György calls out Virginia Governor Spanberger for withdrawing female sports regulation
item.description: Réka György, who lost an NCAA swimming final spot to Lia Thomas, slams Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger for withdrawing a female sports regulation.
item.content:encoded:
Hungarian Olympian Réka György, who lost a place in an NCAA swimming final after competing against transgender swimmer Lia Thomas, criticized Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger’s administration for abandoning a proposed regulation intended to protect female sports and private spaces.

György was one of three female swimmers who petitioned the Virginia Board of Health to enact the regulation last year. The board unanimously approved the petition under former Gov. Glenn Youngkin, but the regulatory action was withdrawn in July after Spanberger took office.

"It’s really sad for me because I had the petition filed a year ago, and Youngkin approved it and wanted to take the next step and protect female athletes and female spaces in Virginia," György told OutKick.

VIRGINIA GOVERNOR ABIGAIL SPANBERGER QUIETLY ROLLS BACK YOUNGKIN'S PLANS TO PROTECT GIRLS' SPORTS

"I don’t like to see that people are using their power, especially political power, to make decisions and hurt other people. And also, it’s coming from a female."

György added that she was "really disappointed" by the decision.

György filed the petition in April 2025 alongside former Roanoke College swimmers Lily Mullens and Carter Satterfield. It asked the Board of Health to adopt regulations preventing biological males from participating on female-only athletic teams or entering female-designated spaces where women and girls could be undressing.

After receiving more than 2,300 public comments, the board voted 14–0 in August 2025 to begin the regulatory process. The Youngkin administration subsequently approved a Notice of Intended Regulatory Action, which was published that November.

SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

However, the Spanberger administration withdrew the action on July 30, after an additional public-comment period had concluded. The withdrawal was not accompanied by an announcement from the governor’s office and was later published in the Virginia Register of Regulations.

The official notice said the State Board of Health would not proceed "upon review of statutory authority."

György questioned why the administration did not call greater public attention to the decision.

"I have a feeling that she’s afraid of the backlash of people, what they’re going to say or think," György said. "Other than that, I don’t know what her motivation is."

György’s advocacy stems from her experience at the 2022 NCAA Division I Women’s Swimming and Diving Championships. The Virginia Tech swimmer finished 17th in the preliminary round of the 500-yard freestyle, one place short of advancing to the consolation final.

Thomas, a biological male who identifies as a transgender woman, qualified for the championship final and went on to win the national title.

"Because the rule-makers let him compete in the women’s category, I got bumped out from the final," György said. "I got 17th, and I wasn’t allowed to swim in the finals. It ended up being me who got knocked out of the finals at night."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

György represented Hungary at the 2016 Rio Olympics and was a two-time ACC champion and two-time NCAA All-American during her career at Virginia Tech. She said she had devoted approximately 18 years to swimming before her final collegiate championship appearance.

"I put everything into swimming that I had," she said. "The 2022 NCAA Championships was my senior year in college, so I was ready to retire from swimming, but before I did that, give my best. I had everything that I was capable of putting into practices to prepare myself to give my best at that competition.

"And the chance to actually swim in the final was taken away."

György also recalled sharing a women’s locker room with Thomas during the championship meet.

"You were in just constant fear," she said. "You had no idea when he was going to enter the locker room."

György explained that putting on a high-level racing suit can take between 15 and 25 minutes, preventing swimmers from simply changing quickly and leaving.

"I was always looking behind my shoulder because I had no idea when my privacy was going to be robbed away," she said. "You try to cover yourself, which usually you don’t do because you are surrounded by other females and you don’t have that issue. But that competition was different."

The experience ultimately prompted György to become an outspoken advocate for sex-separated athletic competition and private spaces.

"I just had this feeling that I had to speak up because, obviously, the people who were in charge of that competition didn’t do anything to protect us females," she said. "One day, maybe I will have a daughter, and I don’t want my daughter to be in a situation where I had to share the locker room and compete against a male."

György, who continues to live in Virginia, joined the petition effort after being contacted about the controversy involving Mullens, Satterfield and the Roanoke College women’s swimming team.

In 2023, members of the team objected when a transgender student sought to join the women’s roster. Roanoke College later said the student had chosen not to compete.

György said she has not yet contacted Spanberger because she only recently learned the regulatory action had been withdrawn, but she plans to seek a conversation with the governor.

"I want to tell her that I hope she sees where I’m coming from," György said. "I hope she sees where other people are coming from when we are trying to protect little girls and females in sports and women-only spaces."

"Title IX was created for a reason," she added. "I really do hope that she is going to follow this rule, and she is going to stand up for women in Virginia."

item.title: Kyler Murray out with concussion so door opens for Carson Wentz as Vikings' new starter – perhaps for a while
item.description: Carson Wentz starts over J.J. McCarthy as Kyler Murray remains in concussion protocol, raising big questions about the Minnesota Vikings' future.
item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Vikings and their quarterback hijinks are at it again, as Carson Wentz will start Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears because Kyler Murray remains in the concussion protocol and J.J. McCarthy remains at the back of the depth chart.

Coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that Murray, who suffered a concussion in the regular-season opener against the Green Bay Packers, is still working his way back to health.

So, it's Wentz time again.

2026 NFL SEASON PREDICTIONS: DIVISION WINNERS, PLAYOFF TEAMS AND SUPER BOWL PICK REVEALED

We say again because the Vikings had Wentz starting last season in Weeks 3 through 8 when then-starter McCarthy was out with an ankle injury.

Wentz went down in Week 8 and that, as much as McCarthy's recovery, thrust the Vikings 2024 first-round back into the starting lineup.

And here we are again. With Wentz surprisingly being promoted from the No. 3 quarterback during training camp, to No. 2 ahead of McCarthy prior to last week's opener, then to the starter on Sunday at Chicago.

And all the while, McCarthy remains on the bench despite having been involved in a competition for the starting job against Murray.

This all suggests things:

It shows the Vikings promoted Wentz because they thought he was more experienced than McCarthy, yes, but also better.

That becomes clear because, again, it is Wentz starting ahead of a healthy McCarthy this weekend.

It also suggests Wentz has an opportunity going forward.

WHY THE MINNESOTA VIKINGS OVER 9.5 WINS LOOKS LIKE A STRONG BET EVEN WITH KYLER MURRAY UNDER CENTER

Wentz took over in the opener when Murray got knocked out of the game on the Vikings' third possession of the game. Murray was down for a time but eventually walked into the team's locker room for a concussion examination which came back positive.

The Vikings were trailing, 9-0, when Murray left and faced a 22-10 deficit with 2:08 left in the third quarter when Wentz threw a TD pass.

And then he threw another TD pass in the fourth quarter.

And the Vikings scored two other times as Wentz completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards with 3 TD passes and without a turnover.

So, Minny beat the rival Packers in dramatic comeback fashion.

O'Connell this week wasn't going to reward Wentz's role in that comeback win by benching him in favor of McCarthy.

But what if Wentz keeps playing well? What if he beats the Bears?

Would the coach bench the quarterback who helped his team get to 2-0 if Murray is ready to play in Week 3?

As ESPN noted, the starter change this week marks the 11th time the Vikings have flipped quarterbacks during a season in O'Connell's five-year tenure.

Yeah, not good.

A majority of those moves came in situations similar to what the team is facing now: An injury to a starter.

Last year, J.J. McCarthy started the first two games but injured his ankle and missed the next five games while Wentz played.

Wentz was then injured in Week 8 and that's when McCarthy took his job back the following week. The Vikings had a 2-3 record with Wentz in the lineup.

If Wentz plays well and stays healthy and keeps winning, the question will loom: Does Murray get his job back even when he's healthy?

item.title: Trump is 'unfettered' and more comfortable with power in his second term, journalists say
item.description: Journalists say President Donald Trump's second White House is filled with loyalists and true believers as the Republican establishment fades.
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK, N.Y. — President Donald Trump is more comfortable on the job in his second term, according to a panel of journalists tasked with covering his every move.

Atlantic reporters Jonathan Lemire, Ashley Parker, Missy Ryan and Michael Scherer discussed what it’s like to cover the White House and other powerful institutions Thursday on stage during the magazine’s annual festival at Perelman Performing Arts Center in New York City.

"We’re seeing someone who completed, arguably, the greatest comeback in American political history. He trusts his instincts and very few others and is sort of an unfettered version of himself," Lemire said.

Lemire said Trump’s second administration is filled with "true believers" and "loyalists," while remnants of the "old Republican establishment" are long gone.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN WAR 'HOPEFULLY' NEARING END AS HOUSE SPEAKER VOWS TEHRAN WON'T GET NUCLEAR WEAPON

"He also is just more comfortable with the job and how to use the levers of power," Lemire said. "That also includes the relationship with the press and how he dictated change in terms of that relationship."

Parker said the presence of chief of staff Susie Wiles has helped, while deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller spent the four years out of power "plotting and planning" how to run a "bigger, stronger, faster, better, more ruthless" White House the second time around.

Scherer agreed, noting that Trump came back with a much clearer idea about what he can accomplish and how it would impact his legacy.

"I was in Dallas last week when he did the midterm convention. His message was, ‘Vote for me one more time,’" Scherer said.

"There's sort of a different, almost nostalgic approach he's taking to things," he continued. "But it is really about, like, ‘This is my last chance to do what I can to get to make my mark.’"

JASMINE CROCKETT DISPARAGES MAGA VOTERS, TRUMP AS 'MOST UNPATRIOTIC PEOPLE'

Ryan, who covers national security and foreign policy, isn’t thrilled that the Pentagon hasn’t held a formal press briefing for months, and staff writer Vivian Salama, who moderated the conversation, said it's harder for journalists to get scoops this time.

Scherer said the lack of leaks from inside the White House showed how it "operates as a unified body" under Wiles.

"The people under her are loyal to her. They're loyal to the president also, but it operates as a functioning organization," Scherer said.

"The first Trump term, there were three or four camps in that same space. They were often warring with each other and stabbing each other in the back and competing for the president," Scherer continued. "It's harder now. It's harder to get inside-the-room details than it was in the first term, but it can still be done."

NEBRASKA SENATE CANDIDATE SEEMS TO CONFIRM AUDIO CLAIMING TRUMP SUPPORTERS' LIVES 'SUCK SO F---ING BAD'

While the second Trump administration has been tighter-lipped than the first administration, Scherer said the Obama and Biden administrations operated like bureaucratic law firms.

"We still have more access here, I think, than we had in recent Democratic administrations, just because they had so much discipline. They had a different ethos about them," Scherer said.

item.title: Lane Kiffin's visit to Oxford isn't the first time a coach made an unwelcome return to his former school
item.description: Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss headlines a history of hostile SEC homecomings, from Nick Saban at Death Valley to mustard bottles at Neyland Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
By now, most of you are painfully aware of the game taking place in Oxford, Mississippi, this weekend between LSU and Ole Miss.

It's less of a game and more a national event, given the added stakes of Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin making his return to Vaught Hemingway Stadium for the first time since leaving the Rebels in the lurch to make his way to Baton Rouge.

There will be plenty of bad blood to go around for all parties involved, but this kind of "reunion" isn't entirely unprecedented.

Prominent head coaches will, occasionally, leave their teams on less than ideal terms, and when they make the return trip to the place they used to call home, it can get a little toxic.

With that in mind, I decided to take a look at a few other times head coaches made their way back to the schools that used to employ them and how those trips compared to Kiffin's welcome committee in Oxford.

MOUNTED POLICE, EXTRA PATROLS AND KIFFIN HATE: OXFORD PREPARES FOR OLE MISS-LSU GAME WITH EXTRA SECURITY

Some of these went a little more amicably than others, but all were fairly noteworthy, so let's dive in.

Before he became the unquestioned GOAT in the annals of college football, Nick Saban was a wildly successful coach at LSU in the early to mid-2000s.

After a pair of SEC Championships and a national title during his five-year tenure with the Tigers, Saban departed for the NFL, leaving many folks on the bayou feeling embittered and betrayed.

Following an unremarkable pair of seasons with the Miami Dolphins, Saban decided it was time to return to the college ranks, opting to don the headset at LSU's biggest rival, Alabama, in 2007.

OLE MISS AND LSU WILL DELIVER CINEMA, BUT THE NEXT WEEK FOR EACH TEAM COULD BE THEIR MOST PIVOTAL TESTS

Tiger fans would only have to wait one year before their former head coach made his way back to Death Valley, as the top-ranked Crimson Tide made their way to Baton Rouge to play 15th-ranked LSU.

The atmosphere around the game was tense and filled with anger and resentment toward Saban, and it didn't help that the Tide escaped with a 27-21 overtime win to effectively knock the Bayou Bengals out of the SEC Championship hunt.

Saban was given a police escort out of the stadium, and years later, the six-time national champion would call leaving LSU the biggest mistake of his career.

Throughout the entirety of the 90s and into the early 2000s, Steve Spurrier and Florida football were synonymous with one another.

The Head Ball Coach won a Heisman Trophy in 1966 while quarterbacking the Gators, and when he returned to roam the sidelines in 1990, he fulfilled the prophecy of "awakening the sleeping giant" once uttered by Alabama legend Paul "Bear" Bryant.

Six SEC Championships and one national title later, and Spurrier figured he had accomplished all he needed to, leaving the friendly confines of The Swamp - the name he gave to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium - for an NFL coaching gig with the Washington Redskins in 2002.

Much like Nick Saban, Spurrier wasn't long for the pros, returning to the SEC in 2005 as the head coach of the South Carolina Gamecocks.

This didn't sit well with a majority of Gator fans, seeing their visor-clad Messiah coaching an SEC East rival, and it made it even worse that he beat his old school in his first year on the job.

When Spurrier and the Gamecocks made their first trip to The Swamp together in 2006, a game with national championship implications for the home team had new stakes attached to it.

While the fans weren't openly hostile towards their former coach (most were even downright warm), it felt almost like watching a weird alternate reality simulation for those in attendance.

The game was an instant classic, with Gators defensive end Jarvis Moss blocking a potential game-winning field goal to preserve the 17-16 win for Florida, and keep their BCS title game hopes alive in the process.

Spurrier once said "only Gators get out alive" when referring to The Swamp, and that very phrase came back to bite him on that day in November 2006.

Hey, look! A familiar face!

Yes, Lane Kiffin is no stranger to making his way back to old stomping grounds, as he had to do something similar just a few years ago.

When Tennessee hired Kiffin in 2009, the then-33-year-old was fresh off of a failed stint as the Oakland Raiders' head coach, and was looking to make a splash in the SEC.

A "splash" is putting it mildly, as Kiffin immediately went into prison survival mode and tried to pick a fight with the biggest guy in the pen, that being Florida and head coach Urban Meyer.

Kiffin ruffled feathers, accusing Meyer of recruiting violations and promising to "sing Rocky Top all night long" after beating the Gators in The Swamp, but after a year of empty promises and a 7-6 campaign, the brash offensive genius left for sunny Southern California to coach the USC Trojans.

Vols fans revolted, burning couches and rioting on campus, while Kiffin left under cover of darkness.

Flash forward to 2021, and Tennessee fans finally got their chance to let their old head coach know how they really felt in person, as the Rebels made their way to Neyland Stadium.

Kiffin had bounced around as an offensive coordinator and head coach at a few different stops before settling into Oxford to coach the Ole Miss football team, and a night game in Knoxville presented an opportunity for some madness.

The game was crazy enough on its own, as the two teams combined for nearly 1,000 yards of total offense and the Vols even had the ball trailing by only five with only a minute left in the fourth quarter.

A controversial review then led to a nearly 20 minute delay, as Volunteer fans chucked mustard bottles and golf balls onto the field, the latter of which allegedly hit Kiffin.

As he was being interviewed on the field following the win, Kiffin did his best George Costanza impression, presenting the very golf ball that struck him to a shocked ESPN audience watching at home.

The fact that this game took place nearly a dozen years after his departure did nothing to snuff out the anger Vols fans held toward their former head coach.

Here's one that a lot of people may have forgotten about, but it deserves mention all the same.

The first three instances on this list are comprised of coaches who decided to stay in conference and take jobs with rival SEC programs, but what happens when a coach who made an unceremonious exit just happens to be on the schedule by way of a cupcake matchup scheduled years before he even agreed to take the job?

For those who need a history lesson, Bobby Petrino coached the Arkansas Razorbacks in the late 2000s and early 2010s, even leading the team to a Sugar Bowl berth in 2010 and a top-five finish in 2011.

He was incredibly successful in the short time he called Fayetteville home until 2012, when he crashed his motorcycle with a former Arkansas volleyball player riding on the back.

This led to an investigation and, eventually, his termination from the university, ending a promising rise for the Razorbacks under Petrino.

A decade later, Petrino found his way back to Frank Broyles Field by way of coaching the Missouri State Bears, a lower-end FCS school.

Arkansas, conversely, was ranked in the top 10 and looked to improve upon their nine-win season in 2021 with third-year head coach Sam Pittman.

It appeared as though the Hogs were going to exact some revenge on their motorcycle-obsessed outcast, but, in a game that may have been a precursor to how the rest of the Pittman era would go, the Razorbacks needed to score 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to eke out a 38-27 victory.

Petrino would actually go on to be the offensive coordinator for Pittman just one year later, and would even be the interim head coach in 2025 when Pittman was given the axe.

They truly can't quit the one that got away in Fayetteville.

item.title: Hasan Piker calls Bin Laden a ‘spoiled brat,’ labels 9/11 ‘blowback’ in Axios interview
item.description: Hasan Piker called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" and labeled 9/11 blowback for U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and Afghanistan.
item.content:encoded:
Hasan Piker, the internet streamer and YouTube personality known for his progressive commentary, called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" for his reasoning in orchestrating the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, which he called "blowback" for U.S. actions in the Middle East in the preceding years.

Speaking with Axios, Piker discussed bin Laden's remarks about why he targeted the United States: U.S. support of Israel, American oil policies and U.S. bases in the Middle East. He noted that bin Laden was once a U.S. ally when the U.S. trained, funded and armed the mujahideen in Afghanistan during the Soviet-Afghan War.

"The action was so heinous and so violent that — and also … given his position as formerly an American ally — I think that he came across a little bit more as a spoiled brat that wasn't getting his way. With many backers in the Saudi kingdom as well and the royal family," Piker said.

CLINTON, BUSH RECEIVED MULTIPLE WARNINGS ON BIN LADEN HIJACK PLOTS BEFORE 9/11, DECLASSIFIED FILES SHOW

The left-wing streamer said he wants fewer actors like bin Laden to "exist in general."

"The other path of least resistance is to not interfere in these affairs in general and not continue to dominate and create an environment where people are going to seek out revenge and put us in a position of danger," he said.

RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORIST COMPARISON

Piker called the Sept. 11 attacks a "horrifying tragedy" and called them blowback for U.S. actions in the Middle East.

"Blowback is not a justification. Blowback is just what it is," he said. "A justification offers either a moral condemnation or a moral acceptance of the act. I do not accept the act of 9/11 morally".

HASAN PIKER INSISTS MIDDLE EAST WOULD BE 'MORE STABLE' IF IRAN HAD NUCLEAR WEAPONS DURING AXIOS INTERVIEW

GOT A TIP?

Piker has faced backlash for remarks in the same interview where he compared the United States to al Qaeda "pound for pound."

"Pound for pound as far as the number of deaths, yes," Piker said. "We have caused tremendous terror all around the world."

item.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel does about-face on TreVeyon Henderson's activism after Russini scandal
item.description: Mike Vrabel's tone on TreVeyon Henderson's social issues advocacy shifted dramatically since April, when the Patriots coach had urged caution.
item.content:encoded:
New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has softened his stance on running back TreVeyon Henderson’s social activism since April, when he cautioned the player to remember that he represents the team.

Vrabel was asked Friday about Henderson’s defense of a Massachusetts couple who say they lost custody of their daughter to DCF after refusing to allow her to transition to a boy.

Authorities have made it clear that the issue had to do with allegations of abuse by the couple, although they have not been convicted of any crime.

TREVEYON HENDERSON EXPLAINS SIDING WITH FAMILY OVER DCF IN CUSTODY DISPUTE INVOLVING GENDER IDENTITY

Henderson spent significant time the past couple of days defending the couple on social media and with beat reporters on Thursday.

And, none of this has really anything to do with football. But Vrabel was asked on Friday how he views Henderson's public position considering in April the coach spoke about there being a "fine line" when it comes to expressing personal beliefs publicly.

"I think he's handled it, I mean, about as maturely," Vrabel said. "I think he tried to explain himself. TreVeyon is a special person, great teammate. I love being around him.

"And I think he pretty much spoke on what he thought and what he believes, and I think that that's impressive. You know, for him to be able to speak on it, and [I] leave it up to him."

So, who is this coach?

He is very different from the one who sat at a roundtable with reporters during the NFL annual meeting in Arizona in April and did not embrace Henderson advocating on behalf of former Chicago Bulls player Jaden Ivey.

Ivey, you may recall, was released by the Bulls after he spoke out against the NBA promoting Pride Month and "unrighteousness."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This is how Vrabel reacted to Henderson's defense of Ivey in April.

"I think there's a fine line," Vrabel said. "I'll tell you, I love TreVeyon. I love the person. He cares deeply about our team. He cares deeply about his faith. He cares deeply about his family. His wife. The people in our building.

"And so, I want them to be able to express what they believe in their heart and in their mind. But also, I want to make sure that they're educated. We want to be inclusive. Everything we want to do wants to provide an environment for people to feel comfortable.

"But also to share their personal beliefs and, also, we represent the team and we represent the organization."

There was none of that get "educated" talk from Vrabel on Friday because perhaps he realized those comments suggested his player didn't know what he was talking about.

And there was definitely none of the "represent the team" narrative from Vrabel because, well, we know why.

Vrabel didn't exactly "represent" the Patriots well during the offseason when it was discovered by Page Six that he spent the days prior to an Arizona meeting with former NFL reporter Dianna Russini at a Sedona resort.

It wasn’t a good look for the Patriots that their married coach was photographed with a married female reporter holding hands, embracing and spending time together at a pool and hot tub.

That entire episode was obviously embarrassing for Vrabel. But perhaps it was also instructive in that he has realized a player taking a moral stand on a topic is not representing the team poorly regardless of whether some people disagree or not.

So, maybe something good has come out of the Russini scandal for Vrabel. Maybe.
